title: Post-Hoc Confidence Rectification via Dirichlet Meta-Modeling for Multi-Task Failure Detection
summary: This hypothesis proposes a post-hoc Dirichlet meta-model that learns to rectify overconfident predictions by modeling uncertainty from a trained classifier's features. The meta-model, trained on pseudo-labels derived from the base model's outputs, generates calibrated confidence scores for both in-distribution misclassification and OOD detection. Evaluation uses OpenOOD benchmarks and compares against post-hoc methods like ODIN, Mahalanobis distance, and OpenMix.
gap: Existing post-hoc methods either address OOD detection or misclassification separately (ref-015, ref-023), or combine both tasks without Dirichlet modeling (ref-062). Ref-042 uses Dirichlet modeling for uncertainty quantification but does not explicitly unify OOD detection and misclassification. No prior work combines Dirichlet modeling with a unified framework for both tasks.
approach: Train a lightweight Dirichlet meta-model (3-layer MLP) on features from a frozen base classifier. The meta-model outputs concentration parameters α₁,...,α_K for a Dirichlet distribution, where entropy H(p) of p ~ Dir(α) serves as the confidence score. Pseudo-labels are generated by applying Gaussian noise (σ=0.1) to inputs and mixing base model predictions via CutMix (ref-038) with λ=0.5. The meta-model minimizes KL divergence between predicted α and pseudo-label distributions.
evaluation: Baselines: ODIN (ref-015), Mahalanobis (ref-023), MC dropout (ref-050), and OpenMix (ref-062). Metrics: AUROC for OOD detection and failure prediction, FPR@95, and Expected Calibration Error (ECE). Test on ImageNet-1K with NINCO (ref-047) and CIFAR-10 with SVHN as OOD. Ablation studies compare entropy-based scores against alternative uncertainty metrics (e.g., predictive entropy, mutual information) from the same meta-model.
